subject.title: Auto-apply safe doctor fixes on gateway start

question: Should Gateway startup ever apply doctor repairs automatically, and if so what exact safe subset, opt-in/default behavior, exclusions, and audit logging are required?
rationale: Current doctor repair can mutate security, auth, plugin, and channel configuration, and the issue discussion includes examples where startup repair changed sandbox and Telegram availability silently; automation cannot choose that security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow opt-in startup repair subset
options.body: Define a small unattended-safe mutation set, require redacted change logging and backups, and keep security/channel/provider/plugin/auth repairs manual unless explicitly opted in.

options.title: Manual doctor only
options.body: Keep startup diagnostics and manual `openclaw doctor --fix` as the supported recovery contract, possibly improving warnings and docs instead of mutating config on startup.

options.title: Run broad doctor repair on startup
options.body: Auto-running the existing repair sequence would address drift fastest but risks silent security and message-delivery changes without a stronger policy boundary.

recommendation.title: Narrow opt-in startup repair subset
recommendation.body: Define a small unattended-safe mutation set, require redacted change logging and backups, and keep security/channel/provider/plugin/auth repairs manual unless explicitly opted in.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signals point to repeated doctor/config recovery work and merged review ownership around the adjacent repair policy.
